title: SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator use first exception instead of last

timeline.message:
SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator use first exception instead of last

Motivation:
SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator implements the promise API and allows for
multiple operations to share a common promise. It currently propagates
the last exception to occur, but this may mask the original exception
which lead to the last exception and make debugging more difficult.

Modifications:
- SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator propagates the first exception instead
  of the last exception.

Result:
Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11161.
timeline.author: Scott Mitchell

timeline.body:
Motivation:
SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator implements the promise API and allows for
multiple operations to share a common promise. It currently propagates
the last exception to occur, but this may mask the original exception
which lead to the last exception and make debugging more difficult.

Modifications:
- SimpleChannelPromiseAggregator propagates the first exception instead
  of the last exception.

Result:
Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11161.
Should we try to add it as suppressed via ThrowableUtil if we already have one stored ?

reply.body: first exception should be sufficient but we can do this if you think it adds value. `addSuppressed` will cause issues with static exceptions (e.g memory leak) and self-references (throws synchronously) so care is required when using this API (e.g. consider enhancing `ThrowableUtils` to avoid adding self-references).
@Scottmitch trying to add a self-reference will throw as Throwable itself guard against it. So I think there is nothing to do in `ThrowableUtil` for us here... I am missing anything ?

> Throwable itself guard against it.

That is what I mean. Throwable's "guard" is to throw in this case, but we generally don't know if the same reference is being used or not. If the same reference in being used and we allow a throw here the async control flow may not  complete (e.g. `Promise.setSuccess` throws before it notifies listeners). For our usages where we don't control the exceptions and need to complete async control flow we should prevent passing a self-reference to `addSuppressed`.
